editorial:
Imagine a home improvement show where the hosts have absolutely no idea what they are doing. That is exactly what you get here. You follow Suzanne, Camille, and Elena as they try to teach you how to fix things around the house, but they are basically dummies. It feels like hanging out with your funniest friends who think they are experts but keep making huge mistakes. Alain Chabat adds a great layer of humor by commenting on the chaos, making the whole experience feel like a giant prank on the viewer.

The best part is watching the confidence these women have while totally failing at simple tasks. The pacing is quick, and the jokes land because the situations are so relatable. It is not a polished production, which is why it works. If you want a lighthearted laugh, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older gem, try searching for a high-quality digital rental on Apple TV or see if you can find a physical DVD copy for your collection to get the best picture quality available.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up with the girls attempting one last big project that predictably goes wrong. Instead of becoming master builders, they prove that being a dummy is much more fun than being a pro. The final scenes show that their lack of skill is the real star of the show. It ends on a high note, leaving you laughing at the mess they made and celebrating the joy of DIY disasters.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves awkward humor and failing upwards.
